judged_text: Google Calendar's token refresh stores the Zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse — an object of the shape {success: true, data: {...}} — as the credential key, instead of the parsed credentials that the replaced googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) returned. On the first token refresh after this deploy (~1 hour in), the stored credential key is silently replaced by the wrapper object while the refresh and the prisma.credential.update both report success; the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation reads credential.key.refresh_token and access_token as undefined, so every subsequent Google Calendar operation (availability checks, booking create/update/cancel) fails with auth errors until the user re-connects. This fires in the default configuration, with the new sync feature disabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (an envelope with `{ success, data, error? }`), not the parsed `data` itself (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, which returns `refreshTokenResponse`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential key is set as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This would store the envelope object into `credential.key` instead of the credential payload shape that `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` previously produced, breaking subsequent reads of fields like `refresh_token`/`access_token` from `credential.key`.
